subject: SignalWave MAP: performance benchmarking plan, access, and close timeline
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kate Larsen <kate.larsen@signalwave.com>, SignalWave Ops <ops@signalwave.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SignalWave MAP: performance benchmarking plan, access, and close timeline

Kate / Ops team —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, attaching a short mutual action plan (MAP) draft and a proposed benchmarking plan so we can lock the last-week-of-April performance window and finish procurement by mid-May. Key asks from our side to make the tests deterministic:

- Dedicated test account(s) with non-prod keys and a sandbox org id
- Network egress rule to allow our load generator IPs (we'll provide CIDR)
- A stable baseline dataset (or snapshot) for repeatable inference runs
- A 3-hour dedicated load window during your low-traffic period (we suggested 0200–0500 UTC)

Benchmark goals we want to validate in the MAP:
- 95th percentile inference latency <= 180ms for 512-token prompts
- Throughput >= 120 reqs/sec sustained at 1k concurrency (TTFT / cold-starts measured separately)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) targets: median <= 60ms after cold start caching priming
- Concurrency scaling behavior and SLO degradation points

I've included a short acceptance criteria matrix in the MAP and a blank schedule for you to pick the window. If you can grant the sandbox account and the temporary keys by Monday (4/5) we can run an initial smoke test on 4/7 and a full load run during the agreed window the week of 4/19.

Attachments: SignalWave_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (draft MAP), bench-plan-summary.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm the preferred 3-hour window and point person for network access? Once we have that we’ll provide the exact IPs, load script, and the DocuSign SOW for signature.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123


From: Kate Larsen <kate.larsen@signalwave.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: SignalWave Ops <ops@signalwave.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SignalWave MAP: performance benchmarking plan, access, and close timeline

Monica —

Appreciate the clear plan. We can do the load window but need to confirm a few internal constraints first:

- Ops prefers maintenance windows between 01:00–05:00 UTC on weekends. Weeknights are possible but require approvals.
- We will need an IP allowlist and a short runbook describing the expected traffic patterns (burst size, sustained qps, headers).
- Security wants the test keys delivered via our secrets portal (we cannot accept keys over email).

I can own the network setup. Can you supply the exact IP list and the runbook by Monday? Also looping in our procurement lead (I’ll forward SOW once we agree the MAP).

Kate Larsen
Director, Infra & Ops | SignalWave, Inc.
kate.larsen@signalwave.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kate Larsen <kate.larsen@signalwave.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SignalWave MAP: performance benchmarking plan, access, and close timeline

Thanks, Kate —

Yep, weekend window works. Attached is an updated MAP (v1.2) with two candidate windows (Sat 04/17 01:00–04:00 UTC and Sun 04/18 02:00–05:00 UTC). The runbook and IP list are below — I’ll get the full load script and traffic profile to you by Monday morning.

Redwood provided items (summary):
- IPs for allowlist: 34.199.120.0/24, 34.199.121.0/24 (we’ll keep these stable for the run)
- Traffic profile: steady-state 120 rps, 1k concurrency target using ramp: 5m warmup, 30m sustain, 10m cooldown
- Payloads: mixed prompt lengths (128/256/512 tokens), 20% long-form generation (>=1024 tokens) for stress on KV cache
- Measurement plan: TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, memory/CPU utilization (agent reported)

Rishi, Karthik — can you prepare the load harness, and confirm whether we should run one full sustained 30m pass or two 15m passes separated by cache priming? Prefer single 30m for stability but open to your recommendation.

Kate — for the test keys, noted that you use a secrets portal; we’ll create a temporary key and deliver via the portal once you share the upload endpoint.

Best,
Monica

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kate Larsen <kate.larsen@signalwave.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 07:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SignalWave MAP: performance benchmarking plan, access, and close timeline

Rishi / Karthik — forwarding Kate’s confirmations and the MAP. Quick asks:

- Can you supply the exact load harness repo link, the docker image tag we’ll run for the Redwood generator, and the expected metrics output format?
- We need a short checklist for the Ops handoff (ports, CIDR, test account id, key name, retention length for logs).

We plan to:
- Smoke test 4/07 (light traffic)
- Full sustained run during 04/17 or 04/18 (finalized when Kate confirms)
- Deliver bench-results-summary.pdf and a post-run MAP update within 48 hours of the full run

If you can drop the repo + checklist by EOD Monday I’ll push the keys through SignalWave’s portal immediately.

Thanks —
Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kate Larsen <kate.larsen@signalwave.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SignalWave MAP: performance benchmarking plan, access, and close timeline

Monica / team —

Attached is the runbook and test artifacts. High-level:

- Load harness repo: https://git.redwood.com/bench/loadgen-signalwave (tag: v2027.04.04)
- Docker image: redwood/loadgen:v2027-0404 (public ECR)
- Default job: 5m ramp -> 30m sustain @ 120 rps -> 10m cooldown
- Metrics export: Prometheus-style endpoints + JSON summary (bench-results-raw.csv attached)
- Recommended passes: single 30m sustained run after a 20m cache priming sequence. That gives more stable p95/p99 values.

Test account stub (do not use in production):
- test_org_id: sw-internal-sandbox-2027
- key_name: redwood-staging-sw-2027-04

Checklist for Ops handoff:
1) Allowlist IPs (provided) and ensure NAT routing for 34.199.120.0/24
2) Provision a sandbox org + temp key entry in your secrets portal
3) Reserve a 3-hour maintenance window and confirm contact for live troubleshooting
4) Ensure 10 min of elevated logging retention post-run for quick diagnostics

Attachments included: redwood-test-keys.txt (key stub), bench-results-raw.csv (sample), runbook.md

I’ll be on call for the run. Ping me if you want us to split the run into two shorter passes — we can do that but it reduces steady-state confidence.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Kate Larsen <kate.larsen@signalwave.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: SignalWave Ops <ops@signalwave.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SignalWave MAP: performance benchmarking plan, access, and close timeline

Monica / Karthik —

Confirmed: Ops will take Sun 04/18 02:00–05:00 UTC as the maintenance window. I’ve created a temporary secrets-ticket (portal ref: SSW-5951) — please upload the test key via the portal and we’ll approve it. Our procurement lead asked that we move the SOW to DocuSign this week; I’ve attached the link below.

Action items (final):
- Redwood: upload key to portal SSW-5951, provide final load script tag and the IPs (for allowlist)
- SignalWave Ops: create the sandbox org and confirm the contact for the run (Ops on-call: ops+oncall@signalwave.com)
- Procurement: finalize SOW in DocuSign (link) so we hit signature by 4/16 and enable billing for reserved capacity

We’re comfortable moving forward on that timeline. Once the run completes, please share the bench-results-summary.pdf and we’ll schedule a post-run readout with engineering.

Thanks —
Kate
